headline: Former Chief Justice Cholendra Rana Arrested From Kathmandu Home, Complaint Undisclosed
dek: Police gave no charge and have not linked the arrest to his four year impeachment saga, which the Supreme Court closed just weeks earlier.
body_markdown:
Police arrested former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana from his home in Maharajgunj overnight into Sunday, according to the Kathmandu Post, Ratopati, OnlineKhabar, Nagarik and several other outlets. Nepali outlets including Ratopati, OnlineKhabar and Nagarik refer to him as Cholendra Shumsher Jabra. A team from the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office in Teku carried out the arrest, a senior police source told multiple outlets.

Police have not said what the complaint against Rana alleges. DC Nepal and Khabarhub both reported that officers gave no details of the case that triggered the arrest. Desh Sanchar and Nepal Press carried the same line. Ratopati and Desh Sanchar reported that a complaint was filed at the Valley Crime Investigation Office, but its contents remain undisclosed.

His nearly four year term as Chief Justice ended in a public storm over corruption allegations that Parliament never resolved. Now the courts he once led will decide whether police can keep holding him.

## A term that ended in crisis

Rana was sworn in as Chief Justice in early January 2019, succeeding Om Prakash Mishra, according to the Kathmandu Post. His term became engulfed in controversy from October 2021, when fellow Supreme Court justices and the Nepal Bar Association accused him of seeking political favors and interfering in judicial appointments, the Kathmandu Post reported.

On February 13, 2022, 98 lawmakers from the ruling coalition registered an impeachment motion against him in Parliament, citing 21 separate allegations of misconduct and corruption, the Kathmandu Post reported at the time. The motion automatically suspended him from office. Parliament never voted on it before the House term expired later that year. Rana retired in December 2022 with the case still unresolved.

The impeachment sat in legal limbo for more than four years. On September 9 this year, the Supreme Court's Constitutional Bench ruled that the motion had lost its purpose and dismissed a related petition, the Kathmandu Post reported. That decision closed the impeachment saga just over two weeks before Sunday's arrest. No outlet has reported any connection between that ruling and the arrest.

## What happens next

No charge sheet has been made public. None of the reports cited here mention his release. No outlet has reported him appearing before a court or facing a formal charge. Article 20 of the Constitution of Nepal requires that anyone arrested be brought before a judge within 24 hours, not counting travel time, so the next test comes fast. By Monday, police must bring him before a judge or let him go.

Until they do, every detail of the arrest itself rests on the same unnamed police sources cited by Ratopati, OnlineKhabar, Nagarik, DC Nepal, Nepal Press and Khabarhub. None of the reports say whether the new complaint is linked to the corruption allegations that shadowed his tenure, or to something else entirely. Readers should treat any link between the 2022 impeachment claims and this new complaint as unconfirmed until police or a court record says otherwise.

key_facts.fact: Police arrested former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana from his residence in Maharajgunj, Kathmandu, in an operation carried out by the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office.
Police have not disclosed the nature or category of the complaint that led to the arrest.
Rana was sworn in as Chief Justice in early January 2019 and retired in December 2022.
On February 13, 2022, 98 lawmakers registered an impeachment motion against Rana in Parliament, citing 21 allegations of misconduct and corruption, which automatically suspended him.
On September 9, 2026, the Supreme Court's Constitutional Bench ruled the impeachment motion had lost its purpose and dismissed a related petition, closing the four year case.

social_hook: A former Chief Justice of Nepal was arrested from his Kathmandu home just weeks after the Supreme Court closed his four year impeachment case, and police still will not say why.
take: A former Chief Justice was arrested at his home on Sunday and nobody in authority has said why. Lawmakers filed 21 allegations against Cholendra Shumsher Rana in 2022 and Parliament never voted. The Supreme Court closed that file on September 9. Now police hold a complaint they will not describe. The Constitution gives them 24 hours to put him before a judge. That deadline is the first real test of this arrest.

nepali.headline: पूर्व प्रधानन्यायाधीश चोलेन्द्र राणा काठमाडौंको घरबाट पक्राउ, उजुरी गोप्य
nepali.dek: प्रहरीले अभियोग खुलाएको छैन। सर्वोच्च अदालतले केही साताअघि टुंग्याएको चार वर्ष लामो महाभियोग प्रकरणसँग पनि पक्राउलाई जोडेको छैन।
nepali.take: आइतबार एक पूर्व प्रधानन्यायाधीशलाई उनकै घरबाट पक्राउ गरियो र अधिकारीहरूले किन भनेर बताएका छैनन्। सांसदहरूले सन् २०२२ मा चोलेन्द्र शमशेर राणाविरुद्ध २१ वटा आरोप लगाउँदै महाभियोग दर्ता गरेका थिए, तर संसदले कहिल्यै मतदान गरेन। सर्वोच्च अदालतले त्यो फाइल सेप्टेम्बर ९ मा बन्द गर्‍यो। अहिले प्रहरीसँग एउटा उजुरी छ जुन उनीहरू खुलाउन चाहँदैनन्। संविधानअनुसार प्रहरीले उनलाई २४ घण्टाभित्र न्यायाधीशसामु पेस गर्नैपर्छ। यही समयसीमा यस पक्राउको पहिलो साँचो परीक्षा हो।
nepali.body_markdown:
काठमाडौं पोस्ट, रातोपाटी, अनलाइनखबर, नागरिक लगायत धेरै सञ्चारमाध्यमका अनुसार प्रहरीले पूर्व प्रधानन्यायाधीश चोलेन्द्र शमशेर राणालाई महाराजगन्जस्थित उनको निवासबाट शनिबार राति अबेर आइतबार लाग्दै गर्दा पक्राउ गर्‍यो। रातोपाटी, अनलाइनखबर र नागरिक लगायतका नेपाली सञ्चारमाध्यमहरूले उनलाई चोलेन्द्र शमशेर जबरा भनी उल्लेख गरेका छन्। टेकुस्थित काठमाडौं उपत्यका अपराध अनुसन्धान कार्यालयको टोलीले यो पक्राउ गरेको एक वरिष्ठ प्रहरी स्रोतले धेरै सञ्चारमाध्यमलाई बताएका छन्।

राणाविरुद्धको उजुरीमा के आरोप छ भनी प्रहरीले खुलाएको छैन। डिसी नेपाल र खबरहबले प्रहरीले पक्राउको कारण बनेको मुद्दाबारे कुनै विवरण नदिएको प्रतिवेदन दिएका छन्। देश सञ्चार र नेपाल प्रेसले पनि उही कुरा लेखेका छन्। रातोपाटी र देश सञ्चारका अनुसार उपत्यका अपराध अनुसन्धान कार्यालयमा एउटा उजुरी दर्ता भएको छ, तर त्यसको विषयवस्तु अझै गोप्य छ।

झन्डै चार वर्षको उनको कार्यकाल भ्रष्टाचारका आरोपको सार्वजनिक विवादमा सकियो। ती आरोपको टुंगो संसदले कहिल्यै लगाएन। अब उनी आफैले नेतृत्व गरेको अदालतले नै प्रहरीले उनलाई थुनामा राख्न पाउने कि नपाउने भनी निर्णय गर्नेछ।

## विवादमा टुंगिएको कार्यकाल

काठमाडौं पोस्टका अनुसार राणाले ओमप्रकाश मिश्रको ठाउँमा सन् २०१९ को जनवरी सुरुतिर प्रधानन्यायाधीशको शपथ लिएका थिए। सन् २०२१ को अक्टोबरदेखि उनको कार्यकाल विवादमा घेरियो। काठमाडौं पोस्टका अनुसार सर्वोच्च अदालतकै अन्य न्यायाधीशहरू र नेपाल बार एसोसिएसनले उनीमाथि राजनीतिक भागबन्डा खोजेको र न्यायाधीश नियुक्तिमा हस्तक्षेप गरेको आरोप लगाए।

सन् २०२२ फेब्रुअरी १३ मा सत्तारूढ गठबन्धनका ९८ जना सांसदले संसदमा उनीविरुद्ध महाभियोग प्रस्ताव दर्ता गरे, जसमा कदाचार र भ्रष्टाचारसम्बन्धी २१ वटा छुट्टाछुट्टै आरोप उल्लेख थिए, त्यतिबेला काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको थियो। यो प्रस्तावले उनलाई स्वतः पद निलम्बन गरायो। संसदको म्याद उही वर्ष सकिनुअघि संसदले यसमाथि मतदान नै गरेन। राणा सन् २०२२ डिसेम्बरमा मुद्दा अझै अनिर्णीत रहेकै अवस्थामा अवकाश पाए।

महाभियोग चार वर्षभन्दा बढी समय कानुनी अन्योलमा रह्यो। यही वर्ष सेप्टेम्बर ९ मा सर्वोच्च अदालतको संवैधानिक इजलासले प्रस्तावले आफ्नो उद्देश्य गुमाइसकेको भन्दै सम्बन्धित रिट खारेज गर्‍यो, काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। यो फैसलाले आइतबारको पक्राउभन्दा दुई साताभन्दा केही बढी अगाडि महाभियोग प्रकरण टुंग्याएको थियो। त्यो फैसला र यो पक्राउबीच कुनै सम्बन्ध छ भनी कुनै सञ्चारमाध्यमले प्रतिवेदन दिएको छैन।

## अब के हुन्छ

कुनै अभियोगपत्र सार्वजनिक भएको छैन। यहाँ उल्लेख गरिएका कुनै पनि प्रतिवेदनले उनको रिहाइको उल्लेख गरेका छैनन्। उनी अदालतमा उपस्थित भएको वा औपचारिक अभियोग लागेको पनि कुनै सञ्चारमाध्यमले प्रतिवेदन दिएको छैन। नेपालको संविधानको धारा २० ले पक्राउ परेको जोसुकैलाई यात्रामा लाग्ने समय नजोडी २४ घण्टाभित्र न्यायाधीशसामु पेस गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरेको छ, त्यसैले अर्को परीक्षा चाँडै आउँछ। सोमबारसम्ममा प्रहरीले उनलाई अदालतमा पेस गर्नुपर्छ, नत्र छाड्नुपर्छ।

त्यसो नहुँदासम्म, यो पक्राउसम्बन्धी हरेक विवरण रातोपाटी, अनलाइनखबर, नागरिक, डिसी नेपाल, नेपाल प्रेस र खबरहबले उद्धृत गरेका उही नामविहीन प्रहरी स्रोतमा नै आधारित छ। नयाँ उजुरी उनको कार्यकालमा लागेको भ्रष्टाचारका आरोपसँग जोडिएको हो कि पूर्ण रूपमा अर्कै कुरासँग हो भनी कुनै सञ्चारमाध्यमले खुलाएको छैन। पाठकहरूले सन् २०२२ को महाभियोग आरोप र यो नयाँ उजुरीबीचको कुनै पनि सम्बन्धलाई प्रहरी वा अदालतको अभिलेखले नभनेसम्म अपुष्ट नै मान्नुपर्छ।

प्रहरीले पूर्व प्रधानन्यायाधीश चोलेन्द्र शमशेर राणालाई महाराजगन्जस्थित घरबाट शनिबार राति अबेर आइतबार लाग्दै गर्दा पक्राउ गर्‍यो। काठमाडौं उपत्यका अपराध अनुसन्धान कार्यालयको टोलीले कारबाही गरेको एक वरिष्ठ प्रहरी स्रोतले रातोपाटी, अनलाइनखबर र नागरिकलगायत सञ्चारमाध्यमलाई बताएका छन्। तर उजुरीमा के लेखिएको छ भनी कुनै अधिकारीले खुलाएका छैनन्।

nepali.notes: फिक्स १० लागू गर्दा वाक्य संरचनामा हल्का हेरफेर गरियो ताकि मिति नदोहोरियोस्, तर स्रोत र आरोपको सामग्री जस्ताको तस्तै राखियो। बाँकी सबै फिक्स दिइएअनुसार सम्बन्धित ठाउँमा लागू गरियो।
nepali.judge: The Nepali misdates the arrest to Sunday night, and the caption both inflates the 21 misconduct and corruption allegations into corruption only and cites an unnamed source without the outlets. Several passages also read as translation and need plain Nepali rewrites.

ranking.reason: A former Chief Justice arrested at his Maharajgunj home is the day's highest-profile story. Ratopati, OnlineKhabar, Nagarik, DC Nepal and others confirm it. It ranks below s2 because every outlet relies on unnamed police sources and the complaint is undisclosed, so it must be written strictly as an arrest on an unspecified complaint.

Confirmed as ranked. The arrest of a former Chief Justice is the day's highest-profile story, and at least five named Nepali outlets report it. It stays below s2 because every account rests on unnamed police sources and the complaint remains undisclosed.

findings.passage: Rana took the oath as Nepal's 27th Chief Justice on January 2, 2019, succeeding Om Prakash Mishra, according to the Kathmandu Post.
findings.problem: The cited source article itself (the same 2026 Kathmandu Post arrest story) reports the oath date as January 1, 2019, not January 2. Separately, sources disagree on his ordinal number: Wikipedia's infobox says 27th, its own body text says 29th, and a 2019 Himalayan Times report at the time of his swearing in called him the 28th. Stating either the date or the ordinal as settled fact sourced to 'the Kathmandu Post' overstates certainty the sources do not share.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the specific article for the date, note that Rana became Chief Justice on January 2, 2019 per the 2021 Kathmandu Post profile, and drop the ordinal 'Nepal's 27th Chief Justice' or flag it as reported inconsistently across outlets.

findings.passage: Nepal's criminal procedure law requires police to either release a detainee or present them before a court within 24 hours, so the next test comes fast.
findings.problem: This is a specific legal claim about Nepali law with no named source in the article's sources list, violating the house rule that every claim traces to a named source. The underlying 24 hour rule is broadly correct but different legal explainers cite different constitutional articles (Article 24 versus Article 20(3)), so the exact citation needs to be nailed down and attributed rather than stated as an unsourced aside.
findings.suggested_fix: Attribute this to Nepal's Constitution or the National Criminal Procedure Code by name, or attribute it to a legal expert or outlet that reported it, rather than stating it as an unsourced fact.

findings.passage: Rana is Nepal's most senior former judicial official
findings.problem: This superlative is not attributed to any source and is not obviously true. Several other former chief justices are alive (for example Hari Krishna Karki, Kalyan Shrestha, Sushila Karki), and 'most senior' is not defined by age, by seniority of tenure, or by any documented ranking.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut the superlative or replace with a verifiable fact, such as 'Rana is the most recent former Chief Justice to be arrested' if that can be confirmed, or simply drop the sentence.

findings.passage: His arrest is likely to dominate Nepal's news cycle regardless of what the underlying complaint turns out to be.
findings.problem: This is the writer's own prediction, not a reported fact, and it is not attributed to anyone. It reads as inserted commentary rather than verified reporting, which the house style reserves for taking a position only when facts support one.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the sentence or replace it with a sourced fact about why the arrest matters, for example noting he is the first former Chief Justice arrested since [year], if verifiable.

findings.passage: the arrest lands weeks after the Supreme Court closed his four year impeachment saga
findings.problem: The dek and body juxtapose the September 9 Supreme Court ruling with the arrest in a way that implies a connection, even though the article later says explicitly that no outlet has confirmed any link between the two. The framing risks readers inferring causation the sources do not support.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short clause in the dek itself noting the link is unconfirmed, matching the caution already used in the closing paragraph.

findings.passage: Former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana
findings.problem: Every Nepali language source in the candidate list (Nagarik, Nepal Press, DC Nepal, OnlineKhabar, Ratopati) refers to him as 'Cholendra Shumsher Jabra,' not 'Rana,' in both headline and body. The article silently picks the English convention without noting the name variant used by its own Nepali sources, which can confuse readers cross checking the original reports.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a brief note on first reference such as 'known in Nepali press as Cholendra Shumsher Jabra' to align with the house rule of keeping names as the outlet spells them.

findings.passage: Police gave no charge, but the arrest lands weeks after the Supreme Court closed his four year impeachment saga.
findings.problem: The dek pairs an arrest of a named public figure with his corruption-tinged impeachment history before any charge exists. Even though the body later hedges properly, a dek is often all that circulates on social media, and this dek alone implies the arrest is linked to the old corruption allegations without any source saying so.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the dek to state plainly that police have not disclosed any link to the impeachment case, so the caution travels with the headline package rather than only in the body.

findings.passage: Will police name a specific offense inside that window.
findings.problem: This sentence is punctuated as a statement but reads as a question, which is a distracting stumble in an otherwise clean piece and undercuts the punchy, varied rhythm the house style calls for.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as a clean declarative, for example: 'That deadline will force police to name an offense, or release him.'

findings.passage: the arrest lands against unfinished accountability questions for the judiciary that outlasted his tenure
findings.problem: This sentence gestures at a broader point about judicial accountability without naming what those unfinished questions actually are, leaving the reader with a vague abstraction rather than the concrete detail the house style calls for by the third paragraph.
findings.suggested_fix: Either name the specific unresolved accountability questions with a source, or cut the sentence.

red_team.summary: The reporting is well sourced across multiple Nepali and English outlets and is careful to flag the central complaint as undisclosed and any link to the 2022 impeachment as unconfirmed, which is the right instinct for a story about a public official's arrest. But several secondary claims slip past that discipline: a swearing in date and an ordinal Chief Justice number that conflict with the article's own cited source and with other public records, an unsourced legal claim about the 24 hour custody rule, and an unattributed superlative about Rana's seniority. The dek pairs the arrest with the impeachment closure in a way that primes a causal reading the body later disavows, which is the kind of gap between headline package and hedged body that creates defamation risk with a named public figure. Fix the date and ordinal citation, attribute the 24 hour rule, and tighten the dek to carry the same caution as the body, and this is publishable.

responses.response: The red team is right that we asserted a specific oath date and ordinal number with more confidence than the sourcing supports. Different outlets give different dates (Jan 1 vs Jan 2) and different ordinals (27th, 28th, 29th) for Rana's Chief Justice tenure. Stating this as flat fact from 'the Kathmandu Post' overstates certainty. We should either verify against the exact article text or soften the claim.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace with: "Rana was sworn in as Chief Justice in early January 2019, succeeding Om Prakash Mishra, according to the Kathmandu Post. Outlets have reported his ordinal number in the sequence of Chief Justices inconsistently, so we do not state one here."

responses.response: Correct that this is a specific legal claim about Nepali criminal procedure with no named source in our sources list. Even though the substance is broadly accurate, house style requires every claim trace to a named source, and we did not name one.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace with: "Nepal's Constitution requires police to present a detainee before a court within 24 hours of arrest or release them, according to legal explainers of Nepali criminal procedure, so the next test comes fast."

responses.response: Fair catch. 'Most senior former judicial official' is an unattributed superlative and it is not clearly true since other former Chief Justices are alive. This adds nothing verifiable and should go.
responses.proposed_edit: Delete the clause "Rana is Nepal's most senior former judicial official, and" and start the sentence with "His four year term as Chief Justice ended in a public storm over corruption allegations that Parliament never resolved."

responses.response: This is our own prediction dressed as reporting, with no source behind it. House style allows taking a position when facts support one, but this is speculation about media cycles, not a fact. It should be cut.
responses.proposed_edit: Delete the sentence "His arrest is likely to dominate Nepal's news cycle regardless of what the underlying complaint turns out to be."

responses.response: The red team has a point that pairing the September 9 ruling with the arrest, even factually stated as sequential, invites readers to infer a link the sources do not confirm. We already hedge this explicitly in the closing paragraph, so the framing earlier in the piece should carry the same caution rather than let the juxtaposition do unstated work.
responses.proposed_edit: In the paragraph introducing the Sept 9 ruling, add: "No outlet has reported any connection between that ruling and Sunday's arrest." immediately after the sentence describing the ruling.

responses.response: The Nepali outlets in our own sources list spell his name 'Jabra,' not 'Rana,' and house style says to keep names as the outlet spells them. We defaulted to the English wire convention without flagging the variant, which could confuse a reader checking the Nepali originals.
responses.proposed_edit: On first reference, add: "Former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana, referred to as Cholendra Shumsher Jabra in Nepali outlets including Nagarik, Ratopati and OnlineKhabar, was arrested from his home in Maharajgunj..."

responses.response: This overlaps with f5 but the dek is the highest visibility piece of text in the article and social sharing will often carry only the dek. It currently lets readers infer a link between the impeachment closure and the arrest that no source has confirmed. That needs fixing at the dek level, not just in the body.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the dek to: "Police gave no charge and have not linked the arrest to his four year impeachment saga, which the Supreme Court closed just weeks earlier."

responses.response: Agreed, this is a punctuation and grammar stumble, a question mark was needed or the sentence should be rewritten as a declarative. It disrupts the clean rhythm house style asks for.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace "Will police name a specific offense inside that window." with "That deadline will force police to name an offense, or release him."

responses.response: The red team is right that this phrase gestures at something without naming it. House style wants concrete specifics, not abstractions, and we do not name what the unfinished accountability questions are anywhere in the piece.
responses.proposed_edit: Delete the clause "It also lands against unfinished accountability questions for the judiciary that outlasted his tenure."

defense.summary: Most findings are well founded and we accept all nine. The strongest fixes are tightening unattributed claims (the 24 hour custody rule, the 'most senior' superlative, the news cycle prediction, and the vague accountability line), correcting overstated certainty about Rana's oath date and ordinal number, aligning the dek with the same caution already used in the body about any link between the impeachment closure and the arrest, noting the Jabra name variant used by our own Nepali sources, and fixing a stray punctuation error. None of the findings required contesting since each identifies either an unsourced claim, an overstated certainty, or a house style violation that a small, targeted edit resolves without reworking the piece's core reporting.

rulings.note: The article's own cited Kathmandu Post piece reportedly gives January 1, and outlets disagree on the ordinal. Flat 'January 2' and '27th' overstate certainty. Soften the date and drop the ordinal in both the body and key_facts.

This is an unsourced legal claim. The right rests on Article 20(3) of the Constitution of Nepal, not Article 24. The defence's 'according to legal explainers' is vague and names nothing in the sources list, so a named constitutional source is needed.
The superlative is unattributed and doubtful given other living former Chief Justices. Cut it.
This is the writer's own media prediction with nothing behind it. Cut it.
Putting the ruling next to the arrest invites a causal reading. The body needs the no-link caution where the ruling is introduced.
The Nepali sources render the name as Jabra, per their Latin slugs. A short first-reference note helps readers cross-check. It must not bloat the lede.
The dek is what circulates on its own, and it currently implies a link to the corruption allegations. The defence's rewrite fixes this and stays under 160 characters.
The punctuation is broken. The defence's replacement overstates the law, though. A court appearance can extend custody without police publicly naming an offense. Use the wording in the edits instead.
The line is a vague abstraction with no source. Cut it and replace it with a concrete why-it-matters line so the third paragraph still does its job.

(f6; sources: Ratopati, OnlineKhabar, Nagarik).

Paragraph 2, last sentence: attribute it. Change to "Ratopati and Desh Sanchar reported that a complaint was filed at the Valley Crime Investigation Office, but its contents remain undisclosed." (sources: Ratopati, Desh Sanchar per sources list).

The paragraph should then read: "His nearly four year term as Chief Justice ended in a public storm over corruption allegations that Parliament never resolved. Now the courts he once led will decide whether police can keep holding him." The second sentence rests on the Article 20(3) custody rule in the edit below.

Under 'A term that ended in crisis', first sentence: replace with "Rana was sworn in as Chief Justice in early January 2019, succeeding Om Prakash Mishra, according to the Kathmandu Post." Do not state an ordinal (f1).
Same section, second sentence: attribute the October 2021 accusations by adding "the Kathmandu Post reported" so the claim traces to a named source (source: Kathmandu Post 2026 background).

Impeachment paragraph: change "The impeachment sat in legal limbo for nearly four years" to "The impeachment sat in legal limbo for more than four years". February 2022 to September 2026 is over four and a half years.

September 9 paragraph: replace "That decision closed the impeachment saga and restored his retirement standing just over two weeks before Sunday's arrest." with "That decision closed the impeachment saga just over two weeks before Sunday's arrest. No outlet has reported any connection between that ruling and the arrest." The retirement standing claim appears in no listed source (f5).
'What happens next' paragraph: replace "Rana remained in police custody as this article was published." with "None of the reports cited here mention his release."

Same paragraph: replace the 24 hour sentence with "Article 20 of the Constitution of Nepal requires that anyone arrested be brought before a judge within 24 hours, not counting travel time, so the next test comes fast." Add to the sources list "Constitution of Nepal 2015, Article 20(3), Nepal Law Commission, https://lawcommission.gov.np" with used_for "24 hour production before court requirement" (f2).
Same paragraph: replace "Will police name a specific offense inside that window." with "By Monday, police must bring him before a judge or let him go." (f8).

Final paragraph: change "every detail beyond the fact of the arrest rests on" to "every detail of the arrest itself rests on". The background rests on named Kathmandu Post reporting, not on police sources.

key_facts: change the third fact to "Rana was sworn in as Chief Justice in early January 2019 and retired in December 2022." Remove '27th' and the exact January 2 date unless the cited Kathmandu Post text is checked and confirms it (f1).
judge_1.reason: The core fact is solidly sourced across many Nepali and English outlets, and the body handles the undisclosed complaint with proper caution. The dek implies a link to the corruption impeachment that no source makes, and several secondary claims are unsourced or overstated. These include the oath date and ordinal, the 24 hour rule, the superlative, the 'restored his retirement standing' line and 'nearly four years'. All of these can be fixed in one pass.

rulings.note: Fixed. The body now says he was sworn in in early January 2019 and gives no ordinal. Key fact 3 matches this and drops the January 2 date and '27th'.

Fixed. The 24 hour rule is now attributed to Article 20 of the Constitution of Nepal. The travel time exception is kept, and Article 20(3) is in the sources list. This matches what Article 20(3) says about bringing an arrested person before a court.
Fixed. The 'most senior former judicial official' superlative is gone.
Fixed. The news cycle prediction is deleted.
Fixed. The no-link caution now comes right after the September 9 ruling. The unsourced 'restored his retirement standing' line is removed.
Fixed. A short second sentence gives the Jabra form used by Ratopati, OnlineKhabar and Nagarik, and the lede stays clean.
Fixed. The dek now says police have not linked the arrest to the impeachment, so the caution goes wherever the dek is shared. It is about 138 characters.
Fixed. The broken sentence is replaced with 'By Monday, police must bring him before a judge or let him go.' This follows the Article 20(3) rule, and it does not claim police must name an offense.
Fixed. The vague accountability line is cut. Paragraph 3 now ends on a concrete why-it-matters line about the courts deciding on his custody.
